title: SeekAndDestroy

panels.title: AI quality and spend - was the answer right, and what did it cost
panels.description:
Whether the platform is producing CORRECT answers, and what they cost. First because a wrong answer returned successfully is this platform's characteristic failure, and every panel below this one would call that healthy.

Spend sits here rather than under operations because cost per answer is a property of the answer, and a model that got cheaper by getting worse is only visible when the two are read together.

panels.title: Number drift: rejected, and never checked
panels.description:
THIS IS NOT A HALLUCINATION RATE, and it used to be titled as though it were. assert_no_number_drift BLOCKS at the request path - it throws, and the answer never ships - so this measures A GUARD FIRING, not an outcome that reached anybody.

TWO LINES, and the second is the one to watch. `rejected` is the guard catching a figure that does not match its evidence. `never checked` is the guard running and comparing NOTHING - every field skipped because it was not numeric, or no evidence key matched its name. Both used to be counted as clean, so this panel could read a confident 0% over zero comparisons.

A rising `never checked` share is a silent failure of the safety property this platform is built on: the evidence keys have stopped matching the field names and nothing is being verified.

WHAT IT STILL CANNOT SEE: an answer where every figure is real and the ATTRIBUTION is wrong - incidents belonging to one cluster narrated against another. Every number matches its evidence and the answer is false. That is a grader question, not a guard one.

The axis is pinned 0-1. It previously auto-ranged to 10000% over an empty series, because a percentunit with no max and nothing to plot will scale to whatever the clamp produces.

panels.title: Fidelity score distribution
panels.description:
A DISTRIBUTION, not a mean. An average fidelity of 0.97 can be 97 perfect answers and 3 broken ones, or 100 answers each carrying a wrong figure - those need different responses and a mean cannot tell them apart.

Fidelity is not scored here when nothing was graded. This panel stays EMPTY rather than drawing a zero, because a fidelity of 0 means every figure was ungrounded - the opposite of 'nothing was measured'.

panels.title: Judge scores by dimension
panels.description:
The LLM judge, kept separate from the deterministic graders on purpose. Graders are arithmetic; the judge is an opinion. Averaging them gives a 'quality score' that cannot be acted on, because a drop could be a fabricated figure or a model being less chatty and only one of those is an incident. p10 matters more than p50 - it is the bad tail.

EMPTY? Check 'Judge verdicts excluded' to the right. Every role defaults to the same model, which makes the judge the author of what it is grading - those verdicts are stored and disqualified, never averaged in. Point the judge role at a different provider on Model Settings and this fills in.

EMPTY IS NOT ZERO, and this panel deliberately does not zero-fill. A p50 of 0 would read as 'the judge rates these answers 0 out of 5' when the truth is that no verdict exists. Check 'Judge verdicts, last 24h' beside it: 0 there means the judge produced nothing, which is why this is blank.

panels.title: Narration checks by schema
panels.description:
Which explanation type is drifting. A rate concentrated in one schema points at that chain's evidence rather than at the model - it usually means the prompt is asking for a figure the evidence does not carry, which is a fixable bug rather than a bad model.

Reads a flat ZERO when nothing happened. It used to read 'No data', which is also what a metric that has never fired looks like - so a healthy system and a broken one rendered identically. No narration was checked in this window - not a drift of zero.

panels.title: Judge coverage
panels.description:
Share of produced verdicts that actually counted. 0% with traffic means the judge is not independent of the authors and no quality opinion is reaching the dashboard at all.

0% AND the liveness stat beside it at 0 means the judge is not running at all - a different problem from 0% with verdicts being produced, which means it is running and every verdict is disqualified.

targets.expr:
(sum(rate(sad_judge_score_count[1h])) or vector(0))
  / clamp_min((sum(rate(sad_judge_score_count[1h])) or vector(0))
      + 3 * (sum(rate(sad_judge_excluded_total[1h])) or vector(0)), 0.0001)

panels.title: Judge verdicts, last 24h
panels.description:
HAS THE JUDGE PRODUCED A VERDICT AT ALL. Nothing else on this dashboard separates 'no traffic' from 'the judge is broken': every quality panel goes quiet in both cases.

0 while investigations are running is the signal. Read it beside Judge coverage: 0 here means no verdict was produced; a low coverage with a non-zero count here means verdicts ARE produced and are being disqualified.

panels.title: Judge verdicts excluded
panels.description:
Verdicts the judge PRODUCED and that were deliberately not scored. Rising here with an empty scores panel to the left is not a broken judge - it is a judge grading its own output, which is disqualified by design because a model scores its own work high.

This panel exists because the exclusion used to be silent, and 'no data' looked identical to 'every verdict disqualified'. Those need opposite responses.

Reads a flat ZERO when nothing has been excluded. It used to read 'No data', which is what a judge that never ran also looks like.

panels.title: Judge failures
panels.description:
A judge that silently stops running leaves every quality panel showing its last good score forever, which reads as health. This is the panel that says the instrument itself is broken.

Reads a flat ZERO when nothing happened. It used to read 'No data', which is also what a metric that has never fired looks like - so a healthy system and a broken one rendered identically. Zero judge failures is the healthy state, and now renders as one.

panels.title: Refusals correctly not judged
panels.description:
Replies with no investigation behind them - a greeting, a refused out-of-scope question - which are NOT judge failures.

These used to tick judge_failures_total, so correct refusals were counted as a broken judge and fed the alert that watches it. Split into their own counter rather than filtered out inside the alert, because filtering there hides them from every other reader of the metric.

Two kinds, and the set is closed by construction rather than by convention - the counter only fires when there is no investigation, and exactly two paths produce that:

  Count         an estate count answered from SQL, no model called
  Conversation  a greeting, a capability refusal, or an ask too vague

Rising here is not a fault. Rising here WHILE the verdict count sits at zero means real answers are going ungraded too.

panels.title: Spend per hour by model
panels.description:
Priced from sad.ModelPrice at the moment of each call, so a later price change does not rewrite history. Calls whose model has no price row appear as UNPRICED - a spend graph reading zero because a model was unknown is worse than one reading low, because the second is visibly incomplete.

Reads a flat ZERO when nothing happened. It used to read 'No data', which is also what a metric that has never fired looks like - so a healthy system and a broken one rendered identically. Zero spend. Read it beside 'Real LLM calls': zero spend WITH calls happening means the calls are unpriced, not that they were free.

Promoted from the operations section 2026-09-06, once every call priced again. It was held back deliberately while deepseek was unpriced - 37 of 63 calls returning no cost - because a spend panel missing the majority of traffic shows a plausible low number rather than an obviously broken one, and a plausible wrong number is the harder of the two to catch.

panels.title: Cost per investigation
panels.description:
The number that decides whether a faster model is worth it. Latency and cost move together when roles are switched, and this is the half that shows up on a bill.

Reads a flat ZERO when nothing happened. It used to read 'No data', which is also what a metric that has never fired looks like - so a healthy system and a broken one rendered identically. Zero spend per investigation, subject to the same caveat as the panel beside it.

Cost per investigation, beside the quality panels on purpose: a model that got cheaper by getting worse is only visible when both are read together.

panels.title: Spend-budget denials
panels.description:
Reads a flat ZERO when nothing happened. It used to read 'No data', which is also what a metric that has never fired looks like - so a healthy system and a broken one rendered identically. Zero budget denials is the healthy state.

A denial is the budget control working. Sustained denials mean real work is being refused, which is a different problem from overspending.

panels.title: Spend by operation
panels.description: WHICH OPERATION COSTS MONEY - which is not the one that burns tokens. Measured over one 100-case golden run: generate_final_report was 50.2% of tokens and 33% of spend; JudgeVerdict was 24.7% of tokens and 51% of spend, because its model's output price is 8.3x the cheapest in use. Ranking by tokens puts the most expensive operation second. Panel 104 is the token view; read them together.

panels.title: Cost and tokens per operation, last 1h
panels.description: The denominator matters: 'expensive because it runs often' and 'expensive because each run is huge' look identical in a total and have opposite fixes. cost/call separates them. Empty rows are honest - a task with no calls in the window emits no series, which is not the same as a task that cost nothing.

panels.title: AI operations - models, fallbacks, latency
panels.description: What the models are doing, and how long they take. A degraded provider shows here BEFORE it shows as a quality problem above.

panels.title: Real LLM calls by provider/outcome
panels.description: Reads a flat ZERO when nothing happened. It used to read 'No data', which is also what a metric that has never fired looks like - so a healthy system and a broken one rendered identically. Zero model calls in the window.

panels.title: Real embedding calls by provider/outcome
panels.description: Reads a flat ZERO when nothing happened. It used to read 'No data', which is also what a metric that has never fired looks like - so a healthy system and a broken one rendered identically. Zero embedding calls in the window.

panels.title: LLM fallback activations
panels.description: Reads a flat ZERO when nothing happened. It used to read 'No data', which is also what a metric that has never fired looks like - so a healthy system and a broken one rendered identically. Zero fallbacks means every primary answered - the healthy state.

panels.title: Fallback activations by provider
panels.description:
How often a primary provider failed and its backup answered. Sustained non-zero means a provider is degraded and the platform is quietly absorbing it - answers are still being produced, by a different model than the one configured.

Grouped by from_provider, which is the metric's ONLY label. It grouped by 'provider' - a label that does not exist - so every provider collapsed into a single unlabelled series and the panel could not answer the question in its own title. The title said 'by role'; the metric is by provider.

panels.title: Narration cache hit rate
panels.description: Reads a flat ZERO when nothing happened. It used to read 'No data', which is also what a metric that has never fired looks like - so a healthy system and a broken one rendered identically. Zero cache events in the window.

panels.title: Model call p95 by task
panels.description: p95 wall-clock per model call, by task. p95 is the right tail here, unlike a judge score where the bad end is low and p10 is the informative one. Reads a flat zero rather than 'No data' before the first call.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, task) (rate(sad_llm_duration_seconds_bucket[30m]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Tokens per task
panels.description: sad_llm_tokens_total carries only {provider, kind} and cannot answer 'which operation burns tokens'. This can.

panels.title: Investigation p95, end to end
panels.description: What the person waited for. Model time is often the smaller part: investigation 132 was 59.7s wall against 6.9s of model time.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, investigation_type) (rate(sad_investigation_duration_seconds_bucket[1h]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Platform - traffic and throughput
panels.description: The web tier. Healthy here says nothing about whether the answers were right, which is why it is last rather than first.

panels.title: Host CPU
panels.description: Whole-box CPU from node-exporter, scraped since d8e5ca3 and plotted nowhere until now.

panels.title: Host memory available
panels.description: Available, not free: free excludes reclaimable page cache and reads alarmingly low on a healthy box.

panels.title: Root filesystem free
panels.description: Docker json-file logging has no max-size on this host, so disk is a real ceiling, not a theoretical one.

panels.title: HALLUCINATION RATE
panels.description: Share of GRADEABLE delivered answers containing at least one claim that could not be traced to the evidence the model was given. Fails on number fidelity, entity fidelity OR attribution - an answer is hallucinated if any of the three does. Denominator is hallucinated+clean ONLY: not_applicable and ungradeable are excluded from both halves, because counting a refusal as clean is how a platform that answers nothing scores 100%. clamp_min is 1, not 0.0001 - with no traffic this reads 0/1 = 0 rather than dividing by a fraction and exploding. Read it beside the verdict panel: 3% of 400 and 3% of 4 are different statements.

panels.title: Verdicts, last 24h - the denominator
panels.description: All four outcomes, so the rate above can be read honestly. ungradeable means a truncated prompt or unrecoverable evidence - the answer may be perfect or invented and this platform cannot say which. not_applicable means nothing was checkable: a greeting, a refusal, a count. Neither is a pass and neither belongs in the rate.

panels.title: Which check caught it
panels.description: Counts CHECKS FAILED, not answers - one answer failing two checks increments two - so this must never be used as the numerator of the rate. attribution_fidelity is the newest and the one the others cannot see: cluster msp-p194, which has zero incidents, was told about four belonging to msp-p204 and dal-p044. Every figure was real and every code appeared in the evidence, so number and entity fidelity both passed it.

description: Operational volume AND answer quality. The quality row exists because the guards that catch a fabricated figure already fired on every request and were recorded only as log lines - the checks were real and the signal was invisible.
